learning_outcomes.text: Can detail and structure the task in a team, prioritize, and implement it in methodical steps.
Can independently develop a complete solution as a team that is quantitatively and qualitatively successful and relevant for the clients.
Can independently familiarize themselves with a new topic and successfully process it independently, combining engineering and economic methods and applying their basic knowledge.
Can develop and understand interdisciplinary connections and handle the interaction of various disciplines, especially technology and business administration.
Are able to verbally explain technical tasks, place them in the context of their field, justify approaches to their solution, and present results.
Can competently discuss the project results, present them convincingly to clients, and document them according to scientific standards.
Master the use of project management methods for solving tasks in groups.

Possess methodological and social competence in areas such as teamwork, communication skills, leadership behavior, creative techniques, time management, and can effectively apply these to solve problems in engineering.

After attending the course, dual students, due to broader experiences from practical phases and the application of theoretical content in companies, are able to delve into the offered topic in greater detail and solve more complex tasks.
Increased methodological and social competence leads to a deeper understanding of team tasks and processes.

syllabus_topics: Processing of a semester-long project task in a team
Selection of a project topic from a semester-changing offer of practice-relevant engineering tasks

Processing of typical, practice-relevant engineering tasks with reference to the study programs of the Faculties of Industrial Engineering and Mechanical Engineering, as well as related engineering application fields
Integration of existing practical experiences, especially from dual study components or relevant operational project contexts, provided they have a technical reference to the project task

Possibility to work on an operational or practice-oriented task as a project topic, provided that the topic, scope, technical level, supervision, documentation, and examination performance meet the module requirements
Ensuring equal learning outcomes, equal assessment standards, and equivalent examination requirements for all students
